قام بإعداد هذا 
 المسـتندالسيد الكيميـائي / على حسن محمود إسماعيل وقـام بمراجعتـــه السيدة 
 الكيميائية/ ذكية محمود سلطان حسن مدير إدارة الكيمياء وإعتماد السيد الكيميائى 
 / مجدى محمد جاد الحق مدير عام الكيمياء ووافق عليه السيد المهندس / إبراهيم 
 محمود حسن المهندس المقيم لمشروع محطة كهرباء طلخا 750 م.و.

تم مراجعة 
 المستند بمعرفة السيد الكيميائى / محمد مصباح مقبل - مديرإدارة الكيمياء 
 والبيئة بقطاع التفتيش ومراقبة الجودة بشركة وسط الدلتا لإنتاج الكهرباء

سمير عبد الجليل مدير عام التفتيش ومراقبة الجودة بشركة وسط الدلتا لانتاج الكهرباء 
ومنسق الشركة لنظام معلومات اجراءات الصيانة ووثق من السيد المهندس / محمد نجيب عبد 
الحى رئيس قطاع التفتيش ومراقبة الجودة بشركة وسط الدلتا لانتاج الكهرباء0

عملية تقليل نسبة الصوديوم والبوتاسيوم من 2مجم/لتر حتى 0.3مجم/لترحيث أن وجود 
 الصوديوم والبوتاسيوم بنسبة كبيرة فى السولار يمكن أن يؤدى فى درجات الحرارة 
 العالية (أثناء الإحتراق) إلى حدوث تآكل ويزداد ذلك فى حال وجود مركبات الكبريت 
 والفاناديوم ويتم الغسيل والفصل بإستخدام فاصل سعته 20م3/ساعه ودخول 
 مياه بنسبة 1% من سعة الفاصل حيث يتم فصل الصوديوم والبوتاسيوم بذوبانهم فى 
 المياه وخروج الرواسب إلى تانك الرواسب.
مواصفات الوقود الواجب توافرها قبل المعالجة

الوقود 
 يكون قابل للفصل ولا يحتوى على مخلفات كيميائية مثل الصودا الكاوية أو 
 مخلفات زيوت

نسبة المياه الموجوده بالوقود الغير معالج لابد أن تكون متعادله 
 ولاتكون مرتبطه كيميائياً بالوقود ولاتكون مستحلبه ولاتذوب فى الوقود

نسبة المياه بعد الفصل تكون أقل من 200مجم/لتر فى الوقود المعالج إذا 
 خرجت أكثر من ذلك يدل هذا على أن المياه فى الوقود الغير معالج مرتبطة 
 ومستحلبه بالوقود

يتم قياس العينات بواسطة اجهزة
 Atomic Absorption AAS spectrophotometer 
 واجهزة ICP

أجهزة القياس يجب أن تكون مجهزة لقياس نسب الصوديوم 
 والبوتاسيوم أقل من 1مجم/لتر
 .(Spectrometer 
 and absolutely salt free laboratory equipment)

يتم نقل السولار بطلمبات النقل إلى الفاصل ثم يتم دخول المياه 
 بنسبة لاتزيد عن 1% من معدل سريان الوقود

نتيجة السرعة العاليه للفاصل يحدث فصل للصوديوم والبوتاسيوم ويحدث 
 ذوبان لهم بالمياه ويقوم خليط المياه مع الوقود بالخروج فى ثلاث 
 مراحل 
 1- وقود معالج 2- مخلفات مياه و وقود 3- 
 رواسب

الوقود المعالج ومخلفات المياه بالوقود يتم خروجهم بواسطة تصميم فى 
 مركز الطلمبة الخاصة بالفاصل باستمرار

الرواسب يتم خروجها على حسب زمن دورة
 bowl ejection

الوقود المعالج يخرج الى تنك التخزين للوقود المعالج إذا كانت نسبة 
 المياه مطابقه وإذا كانت غير مطابقه يتم ارجاعه مرة اخرى الى تنك 
 الوقود الغير معالج

الرواسب تتجمع فى مجمع الرواسب أسفل الفاصل و تخرج إلى تانك 
 الرواسب بواسطة طلمبة الرواسب

items: Injecting water into the diesel feed line to the separator to dissolve the salts.

sections_en.text: This document was prepared by Chemist Ali Hassan Mahmoud Ismail, reviewed by Chemist Zakia Mahmoud Sultan Hassan, Manager of the Chemistry Department, approved by Chemist Magdy Mohamed Gad El-Haq, General Manager of Chemistry, and agreed by Engineer Ibrahim Mahmoud Hassan, Resident Engineer of the Talkha Power Station Project 750 MW.

The document was reviewed by Chemist Mohamed Mosbah Mokpel, Manager of the Chemistry and Environment Department in the Inspection and Quality Control Sector of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company, with the approval of Engineer Samir Abdel Galil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality Control of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company and the Company's Coordinator for the Maintenance Procedures Information System, and certified by Engineer Mohamed Nageeb Abdel Hay, Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company.
Since petroleum materials are used in large quantities, it is essential to take full safety precautions for those handling them, such as:

rows: Wearing the personnel uniform and the appropriate personal protective equipment.
Placing Safety tags on valves and instruments when needed.
Ensuring that the place is equipped with suitable fire-extinguishing means, in quantity and type.

sections_en.text: A process for reducing the percentage of sodium and potassium from 2 mg/l to 0.3 mg/l, since the presence of sodium and potassium in large proportions in diesel can lead, at high temperatures (during combustion), to corrosion, which increases if sulfur and vanadium compounds are present. Washing and separation are carried out using a separator of 20 m3/h capacity, with water entering at 1% of the separator capacity, where sodium and potassium are separated by dissolving them in water, and the sediments leave to the sludge tank.

rows: The fuel must be separable and must not contain chemical residues such as caustic soda or oil residues.
The percentage of water in the untreated fuel must be neutral, must not be chemically bound to the fuel, must not be emulsified, and must not dissolve in the fuel.

The water percentage after separation must be less than 200 mg/l in the treated fuel; if it comes out higher, this indicates that the water in the untreated fuel is bound and emulsified with the fuel.
Samples are measured using Atomic Absorption AAS spectrophotometer instruments and ICP instruments.
Measuring instruments must be equipped to measure sodium and potassium percentages below 1 mg/l. (Spectrometer and absolutely salt free laboratory equipment)
Diesel transfer pumps, horizontal pumps of 44 m3/h capacity.
Air compressor of type Double 2 piston type compressor aggregate with air vessel, pressure 6.5–8 bar, and air tank capacity 150 litres.
Diesel oil separator, horizontal type, capacity 20 m3/h.

Sludge collecting 
 channel
Sludge collecting tank, stainless steel type, volume 5 m3.
Diesel is transferred by the transfer pumps to the separator, then water enters at a percentage not exceeding 1% of the fuel flow rate.

As a result of the high speed of the separator, sodium and potassium are separated and dissolve in the water, and the mixture of water with fuel exits in three stages: 1- Treated fuel, 2- Water and fuel waste, 3- Sediments.
The treated fuel and the water waste in the fuel exit continuously by means of a design in the centre of the separator pump.
The sediments exit according to the bowl ejection cycle time.
The treated fuel exits to the treated fuel storage tank if the water percentage conforms; if it does not conform, it is returned again to the untreated fuel tank.
The sediments collect in the sludge collector below the separator and exit to the sludge tank by means of the sludge pump.

Maintenance Procedures Information System
 | Chemical Treatment | Maintenance Procedures
Document Number: Wtr-057-r0a | Equipment: Diesel Treatment Unit — Procedure: Washing with Demineralized Water
Issued to: Talkha Power Station 750 MW
Status: APPROVED
Approval Date: 31 December 2008
Next Review Date: December 2013
Introduction
A process for reducing the percentage of sodium and potassium, in which sodium and potassium are separated by dissolving them in distilled water, and the sediments leave to the sludge tank.
The water is used in:
Injecting water into the diesel feed line to the separator to dissolve the salts.
Washing and cleaning the separator.
This document was prepared by Chemist Ali Hassan Mahmoud Ismail, reviewed by Chemist Zakia Mahmoud Sultan Hassan, Manager of the Chemistry Department, approved by Chemist Magdy Mohamed Gad El-Haq, General Manager of Chemistry, and agreed by Engineer Ibrahim Mahmoud Hassan, Resident Engineer of the Talkha Power Station Project 750 MW.
The document was reviewed by Chemist Mohamed Mosbah Mokpel, Manager of the Chemistry and Environment Department in the Inspection and Quality Control Sector of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company, with the approval of Engineer Samir Abdel Galil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality Control of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company and the Company's Coordinator for the Maintenance Procedures Information System, and certified by Engineer Mohamed Nageeb Abdel Hay, Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company.
Safety Precautions
Since petroleum materials are used in large quantities, it is essential to take full safety precautions for those handling them, such as:
Wearing the personnel uniform and the appropriate personal protective equipment. | 
Placing Safety tags on valves and instruments when needed. | 
Ensuring that the place is equipped with suitable fire-extinguishing means, in quantity and type. | 
Purpose of Treatment
A process for reducing the percentage of sodium and potassium from 2 mg/l to 0.3 mg/l, since the presence of sodium and potassium in large proportions in diesel can lead, at high temperatures (during combustion), to corrosion, which increases if sulfur and vanadium compounds are present. Washing and separation are carried out using a separator of 20 m3/h capacity, with water entering at 1% of the separator capacity, where sodium and potassium are separated by dissolving them in water, and the sediments leave to the sludge tank.
Fuel Specifications Required Before Treatment
The fuel must be separable and must not contain chemical residues such as caustic soda or oil residues. | 
The percentage of water in the untreated fuel must be neutral, must not be chemically bound to the fuel, must not be emulsified, and must not dissolve in the fuel. | 
The water percentage after separation must be less than 200 mg/l in the treated fuel; if it comes out higher, this indicates that the water in the untreated fuel is bound and emulsified with the fuel. | 
Maintenance Procedures
Sample Measurement Methods
 | Samples are measured using Atomic Absorption AAS spectrophotometer instruments and ICP instruments.
 | Measuring instruments must be equipped to measure sodium and potassium percentages below 1 mg/l. (Spectrometer and absolutely salt free laboratory equipment)
Treatment Unit Components
 | Diesel transfer pumps, horizontal pumps of 44 m3/h capacity.
 | Air compressor of type Double 2 piston type compressor aggregate with air vessel, pressure 6.5–8 bar, and air tank capacity 150 litres.

How Treatment Is Carried Out
